column3: “The gathering of the locust” is rendered “as the caterpillar gathers,” and NASB supplies “men.”
“He will fill” is rendered in the past, “He has filled.”
“Valiant ones” is rendered “brave men,” and “outside” as “the streets.”
“Has dried up” is rendered “mourns,” and “shaking off” as “lose their foliage.”
“Your breath is a fire” is rendered “My breath … like a fire,” following a different reading.
“Sojourn” is rendered “live,” and “hearths of perpetuity” as “continual burning.”
“Uprightness” is rendered “sincerity,” and NASB adds “so that they hold no bribe.”
“Strongholds of cliffs” is rendered “the impregnable rock.”
“A king” is rendered “the King,” capitalized; “a land of distances” as “a far-distant land.”
“Barbarous” is rendered “fierce,” and NASB adds “no longer.”
“Broad of both hands” is rendered “wide,” and “a ship of rowing” as “boat with oars”; NASB adds “One.”
